DESCRIPTION: `BLIND` and `SYNTH` both execute with `current_round == 0`, and `ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings()` stores round data by `round_idx`. The second `process_round()` call therefore overwrites the first round’s findings, duration, adoption delta, and cached cumulative state instead of appending a new phase. In a read-only probe, two completed phases produced `round_results` with indices `[0, 0]`, while `_round_findings` contained only key `0` holding the second phase’s findings. This is deeper than a numbering glitch: it destroys blind-round evidence and corrupts downstream convergence and diminishing-returns calculations.

FINDING_ID: F037  
SEVERITY: 0.92

ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74

REF: [dynamic_management.py:2878](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2878), [dynamic_management.py:2935](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2935), [dynamic_management.py:2956](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2956)  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` appends the current `RoundResult` before calling `update_fingerprints()`. `update_fingerprints()` then builds `prior_finding_ids` from `self._round_results`, so the current round’s findings are treated as if they already existed in prior history. In a probe with a single unique first-round finding, `m1.D_decay` jumped from `0.1` to `0.37`, which only happens because the current finding self-matches as a duplicate. Even if the duplicate heuristic were otherwise acceptable, this call ordering makes the decay signal wrong from the first non-terminal round onward.

FINDING_ID: F038  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
REF: [dynamic_management.py:2042](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2042), [dynamic_management.py:2784](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2784), [dynamic_management.py:2800](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2800)  
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` only examines models present in `responses.items()`. If a dispatched model never returns a `ModelResponse` object at all, it is silently skipped: no `EMPTY`/`TIMEOUT` classification, no failure history entry, no exclusion, no abort pressure. In a 3-model probe with only one response supplied, `failures` contained just `{'m1': None}`, all three models remained active, and every recorded failure rate stayed `0.0`. This means the exact case most likely to happen in production, a missing response, bypasses the entire failure layer.

FINDING_ID: F039  
SEVERITY: 0.84

ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79

REF: [dynamic_management.py:482](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L482), [dynamic_management.py:499](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L499), [dynamic_management.py:2669](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2669), [dynamic_management.py:3008](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3008)  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` recomputes COL scores from `self._models`, the original boot-time `ModelSpec` list, not from the live fingerprints maintained by `DynamicManager`. In a probe, I forced live COL scores to favor `par_static` (`1.0`) over `col_static` (`0.0`), yet `reassign()` still kept `col_static` as `COL`. So the “dynamic” role layer is only dynamic with respect to failure history; capability adaptation never reaches role reassignment.

FINDING_ID: F040  
SEVERITY: 0.81

REF: [dynamic_management.py:910](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L910), [dynamic_management.py:945](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L945), [dynamic_management.py:982](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L982), [dynamic_management.py:2677](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2677)  
DESCRIPTION: The probabilistic feasibility extension is not connected to the actual allocator. `LoadBalancer.solve()` and `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` never consult `feasibility_probability()` or `dispatch_check()`, so the threshold only exists as a manual side-channel the caller must remember to invoke separately. In a probe, a model with `L=100`, `L_std=100` was allocated a 90-token task (`[[1]]`) even though `dispatch_check()` immediately rejected it with `p=0.5398 < 0.90`. The advertised safeguard therefore does not constrain the dispatch plan.

REF: [dynamic_management.py:1994](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1994), [dynamic_management.py:2011](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2011), [dynamic_management.py:2981](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2981)  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler._expected_performance()` always uses the original `ModelSpec.fingerprint` captured in `self.models`, while `DynamicManager.update_fingerprints()` only updates `_live_fingerprints`. The failure layer therefore judges underperformance against stale capability baselines. In a probe after one round, `m1`’s live expected score had moved from `0.75` to `0.711`, but `FailureHandler` still used `0.75`. That makes underperformance detection inconsistent with the adaptation the rest of the manager claims to be doing.

FINDING_ID: F042  
SEVERITY: 0.62

ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57

REF: [dynamic_management.py:2115](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2115), [dynamic_management.py:2456](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2456), [dynamic_management.py:2528](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2528)  
DESCRIPTION: The real-time monitoring interface defines recovery events such as `RETRY`, `EXCLUDE`, and `ABORT`, but `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` never emits them. The PM callback sees the raw failure event, not the recovery decision actually taken. In a probe, an empty response emitted only `('EMPTY', 'm2', 'Empty or null response')`; no `RETRY` event was sent even though the selected action was `RecoveryAction.RETRY`. That makes the monitoring API incomplete for auditing or intervening in recovery behavior.
